p: The Raptor Foundation is based at Woodhurst, a small village a few miles north of St Ives, in the gently rolling countryside between Huntingdon and the fens. It's a compact site, so you can see everything in a couple of hours and still have time for something else. Try to time your visit so you catch a flying display, because seeing these birds in action is the real highlight. There's often the chance to get closer to some of the birds, which is a real treat for budding naturalists.

Wrap up warmly in cooler months, because the displays are outdoors and the fenland breeze can bite. In summer, bring sun cream and a hat. And if you've got a keen photographer in the family, a long lens or a phone with a decent zoom will come in handy.

Huntingdon and the surrounding area have plenty more to offer. The Cromwell Museum, in the old grammar school where both Oliver Cromwell and Samuel Pepys studied, tells the story of the Lord Protector and the Civil War. Hinchingbrooke Country Park, on the edge of town, has lakes, meadows and woodland to explore. A little further along the Great Ouse, Houghton Mill is a working watermill run by the National Trust, set in lovely riverside meadows. St Ives has a rare medieval bridge with a chapel built into it, one of only a handful left in England. Grafham Water, west of Huntingdon, is a big reservoir with cycling and walking routes all the way round, while Paxton Pits nature reserve, near St Neots, is a haven for birdwatchers keen to spot wild species too.
